as a single fraction in its simplest form.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:

M1: Use of common denominator - combines three fractions to form one. The denominator must be correct for their fractions and at least one numerator must have been adapted.
A1: Correct simplified intermediate answer, e.g. $\frac{4x-6}{(2x+3)(2x-3)}$. It must be a correct $\frac{\text{Linear}}{\text{Quadratic}}$.

parts.label: i(a)
parts.text:
(i) (a) Show that $2\tan x - \cot x = 5\csc x$ may be written in the form
$a\cos^2 x + b\cos x + c = 0$
stating the values of the constants $a$, $b$ and $c$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: $2\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}-\frac{\cos x}{\sin x}=\frac{5}{\sin x}$
M1: Uses common denominator to give $2\sin^2 x - \cos^2 x = 5\cos x$
M1: Replaces $\sin^2 x$ by $(1-\cos^2 x)$ to give $2(1-\cos^2 x)-\cos^2 x = 5\cos x$
A1: Obtains $3\cos^2 x + 5\cos x - 2 = 0$ ($a=3,\ b=5,\ c=-2$)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1: Uses definitions $\tan x=\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}$, $\cot x=\frac{\cos x}{\sin x}$ and $\text{cosec}x=\frac{1}{\sin x}$. Condone $5\text{cosec}x=\frac{1}{5\sin x}$ as the intention is clear. Alternatively uses $\cot x=\frac{1}{\tan x}$ and $\text{cosec}x=\frac{1}{\sin x}$ to write the equation in terms of $\tan x$ and $\sin x$. This may be implied by later work that achieves $A\tan^2 x\pm B=C\sec x$
- M1: Either uses common denominator and cross multiples, or multiplies each term by $\sin x\cos x$ to achieve an equation of the form equivalent to $A\sin^2 x\pm B\cos^2 x=C\cos x$. It may be seen on the numerator of a fraction. Alternatively multiplies by $\tan x$ to achieve $A\tan^2 x\pm B=C\sec x$
- M1: In the alternative uses $\tan^2 x=\sec^2 x-1$ to form a quadratic in sec x, followed by $\sec x=\frac{1}{\cos x}$ to form a quadratic equation in terms of $\cos x$. A1: Obtains $\pm K(3\cos^2 x+5\cos x-2)=0$

parts.label: ii
parts.text:
(ii) Show that
$\tan\theta + \cot\theta \equiv \lambda \csc 2\theta, \quad \theta \neq \frac{n\pi}{2},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}$
stating the value of the constant $\lambda$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: $\tan\theta + \cot\theta \equiv \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}+\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}$ (or equivalent using a matching definition of $\cot$)
M1: Uses common denominator to write as a single fraction, $\equiv \frac{\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}$
M1: Uses identities $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1$ and $\sin 2\theta = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta$ specifically to achieve an expression of the form $\frac{\lambda}{\sin 2\theta}$
A1: $\equiv 2\csc 2\theta$ (so $\lambda = 2$). Achieves printed answer with no errors.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1: Acceptable answers are $\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}+\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}$, $\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}+\frac{1}{\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}}$, $\tan\theta+\frac{1}{\tan\theta}$. Condone a miscopy on the sign. Eg Allow $\tan\theta-\frac{1}{\tan\theta}$
- M1: In the examples given above, example 2 would need to be inverted. The denominator has to be correct and one of the terms must be adapted.
- M1: Alternatively uses $1+\tan^2\theta=\sec^2\theta=\frac{1}{\cos^2\theta}$, $\tan\theta=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$ and $\sin 2\theta=2\sin\theta\cos\theta$ specifically to achieve an expression of the form $\frac{\lambda}{\sin 2\theta}$. A line of $\frac{1}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}$ achieved on the lhs followed by $\lambda=\frac{1}{2}$ or 2 would imply this mark
- Or: $\tan\theta+\cot\theta\equiv\tan\theta+\frac{1}{\tan\theta}$ B1; $\equiv\frac{\tan^2\theta+1}{\tan\theta}$ M1; $\equiv\frac{1}{\cos^2\theta\times\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}}\equiv\frac{2}{\sin 2\theta}$ M1; $\equiv 2\text{cosec}2\theta$ (so $\lambda=2$) A1
- $\tan\theta+\cot\theta=\lambda\text{cosec}2\theta\Rightarrow\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}+\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}=\frac{\lambda}{\sin 2\theta}=\frac{\lambda}{2\sin\theta\cos\theta}$ B1; $\times 2\sin\theta\cos\theta\Rightarrow 2\sin^2\theta+2\cos^2\theta=\lambda$ M1; Factorises $2(\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta)=\lambda\Rightarrow 2=\lambda$ M1; All above correct + a statement like 'hence true', 'QED' A1
- Allow for a different variable as long as it is used consistently.
